grounding.excerpt: *10     The limits begin on the effective date of this permit and lasting through 3 years from the permit effective date.
*11     The limits apply during the period beginning 3 year from the permit effective date
This permit shall become effective on December 1, 2021. This permit and the authorization to discharge shall expire at midnight, November 30, 2026.

rationale: The obligation values name permit, outfall, parameter, and period_universe but do not state which named numeric limit regime is the subject of limit_regime_applies, so there is no complete regime-interval pairing to adjudicate under the oracle contract. The packet establishes two sequential TDS net-increase limits—27,664 lbs/day under footnote *10 (effective date through three years) and 24,992 lbs/day under footnote *11 (beginning three years from the effective date)—with a permit effective date of December 1, 2021. Three years from that date is approximately December 1, 2024, while FY2025 runs October 1, 2024 through September 30, 2025. That window straddles the regime boundary: October–November 2024 falls under the first limit and December 2024–September 2025 under the second. The packet therefore does not establish that a single named regime governs the entire FY2025 monthly monitoring period_universe, nor does it identify which candidate regime the obligation asserts. ACCEPT cannot be grounded without a stated pairing; REJECT is not warranted because enforceable limits clearly apply during portions of FY2025. Neither burden for semantic closure is met.
